column1: # Reviewed exceptions for scripts/guard-pdb-selector-match.sh (#3596).
# One row per PodDisruptionBudget whose pods nothing in this repository renders, in ONE cluster.
# Seven tab-separated columns:
#   <cluster>
column7: <where the pod labels come from, and where they were verified>

column1: # <cluster> is the overlay under k8s/clusters/ the row applies to. It applies to no other: the
# same budget in a second cluster is judged there, and needs its own row to be excepted there.
# <producer> is what builds the pods:
#   <Kind>/<namespace>/<name>   an object the same cluster renders, from which a controller builds the
#                               workload at runtime. The guard requires it to be rendered. A
#                               HelmRelease is accepted only while the guard cannot render its chart,
#                               and only when it is installed into the budget's namespace. A workload
#                               kind (Deployment, StatefulSet, ...) is refused: the guard reads those.
#   external:<what>             something outside every render, such as the node OS.
# <pin> is where the version the labels were verified at is pinned, and <verified version> is its
# value on the day they were verified:
#   HelmRelease/<namespace>/<name>   spec.chart.spec.version of that HelmRelease, as the cluster renders it
#   file:<path>:<.dotted.path>       a value in a YAML file, the path taken from the repository root
# The guard reads the pin and fails while it differs from the verified version, so a bump cannot
# merge until the labels have been verified again at the new version and the row updated.
# <unrelated workloads> is `-`, or a comma-separated list of <Kind>/<name>. The guard refuses a row
# while the cluster renders, into the budget's namespace, a workload that carries part of what the
# selector names (one of its matchLabels, In or Exists requirements): that workload can be judged,
# and it does not match. Naming it here is the reviewed statement that it is a different workload
# sharing a label, not the one the budget was written for. Never list the budget's own workload: if
# the cluster renders that, fix the selector and remove the row. A name that stops applying fails.
# A row is a tracked disposition, never an approval of a mismatch: the guard cannot check the
# selector of a budget listed here against its pods. A row is also refused when the budget has no
# selector and when its producer does not hold. A row for a budget that a rendered workload
# satisfies, that its cluster does not render, or for a cluster that is no overlay, fails the
# guard, so remove it then.
prod
column7: Talos installs the CoreDNS Deployment from its own bootstrap manifests, so no layer of the prod cluster renders it. Pod label k8s-app=kube-dns verified in the Talos source, internal/app/machined/pkg/controllers/k8s/internal/k8stemplates/coredns.go.

column7: coroot-operator builds the coroot-coroot StatefulSet from this custom resource at runtime; its chart renders only the operator. Pod labels managed-by=coroot-operator, part-of=<resource name> and component=coroot verified in the coroot-operator source (app version v1.10.5), controller/controller.go Labels and controller/coroot.go. The crossplane-sync-exporter Deployment is this repository's own metrics exporter; it shares only the grouping label part-of=coroot.
